title: The Roads to the Emerald City
tagline: Follow the brick, read the land, choose the way a person can actually walk
description: Dorothy must cross an unfamiliar country divided into four coloured regions. Baum's Oz becomes a true map skills course: compass and direction, legend and symbols, scale and winding distance, regions and borders, barriers and route choice, and a final pair of sketch maps a stranger can follow.
worldPrompt: An original mapmaker's adventure across L. Frank Baum's Oz (The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, 1900, public domain). The learner travels with Dorothy, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion from Munchkin Country to the Emerald City. Each chapter gates the geography unit: directions with the compass rose, symbols and legend, scale bar and winding distance, regions as Munchkin, Winkie, Gillikin, and Quadling countries, and barriers versus route choice. Characters are Dorothy, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Lion, and the Wizard only. The Scarecrow puzzles directions, the Woodman guards care over the road, the Lion tests courage at the barrier. No new Oz characters invented. Loot is wayfinding gear: compass, road tile, legend card, scale ruler, pass token.

characters.name: Dorothy
characters.bio: Carried far from Kansas, observant and practical. You walk in her sensible shoes and read the map before you move.

characters.name: Scarecrow
characters.bio: Wants brains more than anything. He is brilliant at directions and checks the compass twice.

characters.name: Tin Woodman
characters.bio: Careful and kind. He keeps the road's edges, bridges, and legend tidy.

characters.name: Lion
characters.bio: Loud worry, deep courage. He steps up at the mountain pass and tests the barrier choice.

characters.name: Wizard
characters.bio: Kind in the final telling, smaller than his legend. He stamps a map that strangers can follow.

chapters.title: Which Way Is West?
chapters.hook: Munchkin Country to the Emerald City, but the Scarecrow points the wrong way.

chapters.title: What the Map Means
chapters.hook: A dot, a line, a colour patch. Without the key they are just pictures.

chapters.title: How Far Is Far?
chapters.hook: One centimetre stands for ten kilometres. The brick road does not run straight.

chapters.title: Four Countries, One Land
chapters.hook: Blue east, yellow west, purple north, red south, and green at the heart.

chapters.title: The Pass or the Long Way Round
chapters.hook: Straight over the mountains or winding around them. The short draw can be the long walk.

chapters.title: Draw It So a Stranger Finds It
chapters.hook: Oz and home, each with title, arrow, legend, bar, and border a test walker can check.

loot.name: Compass Rose
loot.description: The rose that settles Never Eat Soggy Waffles: N, E, S, W and the points between. Chapter 1, Munchkin Country.

loot.name: Yellow Brick
loot.description: One brick from the winding road. Reminds you to measure along curves, not straight jumps. Chapter 1-2, the brick road.

loot.name: Legend Card
loot.description: The key that promises each symbol means one thing everywhere on the map. Chapter 2, the legend.

loot.name: Scale Ruler
loot.description: One centimetre to ten kilometres. Multiplies a short line into the real walk. Chapter 3, the scale bar.

loot.name: Pass Token
loot.description: Stone chip from the chosen valley route. Proof the best path is the one a person can walk. Chapter 5, the mountains.

loot.name: Cartographer's Seal
loot.description: The Wizard's own stamp on a pair of maps a stranger actually followed. Legendary wayfinding clear.
